findings.section: Amazon RDS runs the database engine while you keep the queries (3 min); bullets 3.3.S3, 4.3.S2, 3.3.K6
findings.quote: 1. **Choose an engine.** RDS offers [IBM Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server](../facts/rds.md#rds-engines-supported), [MySQL, Oracle Database, and PostgreSQL](../facts/rds.md#rds-engines-supported).
findings.evidence: Bullets 3.3.S3 and 4.3.S2 ('Determining an appropriate database engine (for example, MySQL compared with PostgreSQL)') and 3.3.K6 ('Database engines with appropriate use cases') are mapped to this subsection in brief.json, but it only lists the six engines; no section says what differs between them. FREQUENCY.md row 7 lists 'MySQL vs PostgreSQL' among the reported RDS sub-topics. Quiz Question 18 (rds-q018) tests a MySQL-versus-PostgreSQL difference that the prose never teaches. Verified facts are ready: rds-replica-mysql-logical-writable, rds-replica-postgresql-not-writable, rds-multi-az-cluster-engines-mysql-postgresql, rds-read-replica-cascading-engines, rds-blue-green-engines-only, rds-encryption-tde-oracle-sqlserver. Add a short 'engine differences that decide answers' table (feature x engine) with these facts.
findings.resolution: fix-26 (partly, within the 4,500-word limit of 2-deep.md): the two differences that the shipped items test are now taught. A Go deeper block 'a writable replica' in the read replica subsection ([read replica to be writable] for MySQL or MariaDB; PostgreSQL does not allow a replica [to be made writable]) backs q018 and c026; Multi-AZ DB cluster step 4 states that clusters run RDS for MySQL and RDS for PostgreSQL (backs c008 and the new Check 1). A full feature x engine table did not fit.

findings.quote: **Review.** [A Multi-AZ DB instance copies every write to a standby synchronously](2-deep.md#a-multi-az-db-instance-copies-every-write-to-a-standby-synchronously-4-min)
findings.evidence: The key is an RDS Blue/Green Deployment, but 2-deep.md never mentions Blue/Green Deployments; the Review section only has the trap that an engine upgrade causes downtime even with Multi-AZ. Card rds-c019 also tests it. Add one step or a sentence after the trap with rds-blue-green-staging-in-sync and rds-engine-upgrade-downtime-blue-green (both verified), and a signal row 'major version upgrade, test on a synced copy, minimal downtime' -> Blue/Green.
findings.resolution: fix-26: the Multi-AZ DB instance trap now ends 'You can minimize it [using a blue/green deployment]: a copy that [stays in sync with the current production environment].' (rds-engine-upgrade-downtime-blue-green, rds-blue-green-staging-in-sync). That is the subsection q019 reviews. No signal row added: the 1-fast signals table is at its maximum of 8 rows.

findings.section: Extended, Question 14 (rds-q017), Review link; 2-deep.md Numbers A-list
findings.quote: | [7 consecutive days](../facts/rds.md#rds-stop-max-seven-days) | Longest stop of a DB instance | Then RDS starts it again |

findings.section: Manual snapshots stay until you delete them and can leave the Region (4 min), Exam trap
findings.quote: You can [share manual DB snapshots](../facts/rds.md#rds-snapshots-copy-both-share-manual), so you start by [copying the automated snapshot](../facts/rds.md#rds-share-automated-copy-first).
findings.evidence: Sharing an encrypted snapshot with another account is a common exam case, and the deciding fact is missing: rds-share-default-kms-key-not-shareable (verified: 'You can't share a snapshot encrypted with the default KMS key (the AWS managed key) ... create a customer managed key ... and give the other account access to it'). The brief slot 1.3.S2 'share-encrypted-snapshot-cross-account' lost its question (rds-q020 rejected), and only card rds-c030 carries the point. Add it to this trap and to the 1-fast signals table.
findings.resolution: fix-26: the snapshot trap now adds 'A snapshot [encrypted using the default KMS key] cannot be shared: copy it [using the customer managed key].' (rds-share-default-kms-key-not-shareable), and card c030 reviews this subsection. The 1-fast signals table is at its maximum of 8 rows, so no row was added there.

findings.section: Signals and traps, row "too many connections, Lambda functions"
findings.quote: | "too many connections, Lambda functions" | RDS Proxy | it keeps a [smaller number of long-lived connections](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-candidate-too-many-connections) | latency matters more than pooling: connect directly |
findings.evidence: The guard does not name the stem phrase that flips real questions. The chapter's own twin pair flips on it: Question 16 ('too many connections errors at low CPU use' -> RDS Proxy) versus Question 17 ('CPU use near 90 percent ... connections stays low' -> read replica), and trap rds-trap-proxy-reduces-query-load. Guard: 'the CPU is high from reads and connections are few: a read replica'. Keep the latency case for Question 15 as a second clause if wanted.
findings.resolution: fix-26: the guard is now 'reads drive the CPU and connections are few: a read replica', and Recap 2's answer matches it. The latency case stays in Check 3 and in the 2-deep trap rds-trap-proxy-for-every-database (the old Question 15, rds-q021, was retired, see exam-10).

findings.section: Signals and traps, row "highly available, automatic failover, survive an AZ failure"; also 2-deep.md Multi-AZ DB cluster subsection
findings.quote: | the standbys must also serve reads: a Multi-AZ DB cluster |
findings.evidence: A Multi-AZ DB cluster exists only for RDS for MySQL and RDS for PostgreSQL (rds-multi-az-cluster-engines-mysql-postgresql, verified: 'Multi-AZ DB clusters aren't available with the following engines'). Neither the signal nor the 2-deep.md subsection says so; only the takeaway of Question 1 mentions 'on MySQL or PostgreSQL'. A stem with RDS for SQL Server or Oracle that asks for readable standbys makes this guard pick an impossible option. Add the engine limit to the cluster subsection and to the guard.
findings.resolution: fix-26: guard now 'the standbys must also serve reads: a Multi-AZ DB cluster (MySQL or PostgreSQL)'; 2-deep.md cluster subsection step 4 'Two engines. Multi-AZ DB clusters run RDS for MySQL and RDS for PostgreSQL.' Grounded in verified rds-multi-az-cluster-engines-mysql-postgresql; it is not linked in prose because its only display ('aren't available with the following engines') is a contraction, which L803 bans in prose (the card c008 extra links it; request fr-0088 asks for a contraction-free display). findings.section: Storage autoscaling grows storage before it fills but never shrinks it (3 min); 1-fast.md signal "unpredictable storage growth"
findings.quote: | "unpredictable storage growth" | storage autoscaling | [it automatically scales up your storage](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-unpredictable) | the growth is planned: grow storage by hand |
findings.evidence: Verified fact rds-storage-autoscaling-large-loads: 'Storage autoscaling cannot completely prevent storage-full situations during large data loads, because further storage modifications must wait for storage optimization and are limited in number per day.' The heading ('grows storage before it fills') and the signal promise more than that. Add this fact as a step or Go deeper line, and as the guard: 'a large one-time data load: allocate the storage before the load'.
findings.resolution: fix-26: the 1-fast guard is now 'a large one-time data load: allocate the storage first'. In 2-deep.md the trigger step now names the third condition (the last change must finish optimizing). The large-loads fact was not linked in prose: its only display has a contraction (L803); request fr-0088.

findings.quote: - Put Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the DB instance, because every RDS database needs a proxy to pool its connections.
findings.evidence: Three of three distractors are easy to drop: this one repeats the strawman of the stem ('An architect proposes Amazon RDS Proxy for every database') with an absolute 'every'; 'Move the application to AWS Lambda functions that open a new database connection in each invocation' is not a fix for anything in the stem; 'Create a read replica ... move the connection pool' fails on a write workload. A difficulty 3 item needs distractors with real misconceptions, for example 'RDS Proxy to cut failover time' (true benefit, wrong need) or 'a larger instance class for more max_connections'.

findings.section: On failover RDS points the same endpoint at the standby (4 min), Exam signal
findings.quote: > **Exam signal:** "reconnect automatically after a failover" points to the DNS endpoint, and AWS advises you to [implement database connection retry at the application layer](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-cname-flip-retry).
findings.evidence: No exam option is 'the DNS endpoint'; the stems that use this phrase choose between retry logic with a short DNS TTL and RDS Proxy (Question 5 and its twin line). Make the signal 'reconnect faster after a failover, no code change' -> RDS Proxy, but not if 'must connect directly' -> retry and a DNS TTL under 30 seconds (rds-bp-dns-ttl-under-30-seconds).
findings.resolution: fix-26: the signal now reads '"reconnect automatically after a failover" points to retry logic: AWS advises you to [implement database connection retry at the application layer].' The proxy signal of the next RDS Proxy subsection covers the no-code-change case, and the Stop and answer reveal now gives the [less than 30 seconds] DNS cache advice.

findings.section: On failover RDS points the same endpoint at the standby (4 min), step 1
findings.quote: 1. **RDS detects the failure.** For example, [Loss of network connectivity to primary](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-multiaz-failover-triggers) or a zone outage.
findings.evidence: The reverse case is a known trap and is only on card rds-c021: rds-multi-az-no-failover-db-operations (verified: Multi-AZ does 'not fail over automatically in response to database operations such as long-running queries, deadlocks or database corruption errors'). One sentence here would back the card.
findings.resolution: fix-26: step 1 adds 'It does not fail over for [long running queries, deadlocks, or database corruption errors].' (rds-multi-az-no-failover-db-operations).

findings.section: RDS Proxy shares a small pool of connections among many clients (4 min)
findings.quote: 3. **The proxy pools.** RDS Proxy lets applications [pool and share database connections](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-definition-pool-share) and [keeps a smaller number of connections open](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-multiplexing-fewer-db-connections).
findings.evidence: Exam stems with Lambda and RDS Proxy often add 'no database credentials in code' or 'rotate credentials'. The chapter never mentions IAM database authentication or Secrets Manager with RDS, although verified facts exist (rds-proxy-iam-and-secrets-auth, rds-proxy-lambda-connection-pooling quote 'You can take advantage of any IAM authentication you already have for Lambda functions', rds-sec-bp-secrets-manager-rotation) and card rds-c008 tests the IAM token lifetime. One step, or an xref to chapter 07, would cover it.
findings.resolution: fix-26 (note): not added to 2-deep.md, which is at its 4,500-word limit after the blocking and should fixes. The orphaned card rds-c008 (IAM token lifetime) was replaced, so no item tests untaught IAM authentication; the rds-s03 follow-up already pairs RDS Proxy with Secrets Manager and IAM authentication for Lambda. Left for the security chapters or a later pass.
